hook: SCP-609 is a green pool ball that exists as an idea, sold as a children's toy by Dr. Wondertainment. The packaging copy is a stack of philosophy puns, so read it aloud in your head; the joke and the danger turn out to be the same thing.
whyItMatters:
The file is a playful take on Plato's theory of forms: the ball cannot be damaged or erased because it is the perfect original that every other pool ball merely copies. That premise turns a cute toy into a Keter, since anyone who looks at it can move or multiply it just by thinking.

It also shows the Wondertainment style at its most cheerful and most careless, with legal disclaimers that admit, in a sunny voice, that the product may ruin your sense of what is real.
thingsToNotice:
Watch the containment logic: because thinking about the ball is enough to summon a copy, the procedures lean on keeping minds calm and eyes away, and the ironic-process problem means trying not to think of it is exactly what goes wrong. The recovery list escalates from a kitchen and a bathroom to a TV set, a researcher's frontal lobe and breast tissue, and finally the Moon, where it is still stuck.

The twist is that the box never held the ball at all. What it held was the assembly guide, a dense booklet written like the ravings of someone in deep distress, and reading it all teaches you to make the ball yourself. Amnestics cannot remove that ability; they can only make you forget you have it until something green, round or numbered six reminds you.
